steps.label: Fire particles one at a time at two narrow slits
steps.sub: A detector screen behind the wall records where each one lands

steps.label: Classical bullets would give two bright bands
steps.sub: Instead, an interference pattern of alternating bright and dark bands builds up

steps.label: This happens even with huge gaps between particles
steps.sub: No particle can be bumping into another — yet the pattern still appears

steps.label: Each single particle still lands as one localized dot
steps.sub: Particle-like at detection; wave-like in the pattern built from many dots

steps.label: Add a detector that reveals which slit each particle used
The interference pattern vanishes immediately
steps.sub: Replaced by the plain two-band pattern classical bullets would give

steps.label: It isn't about the detector disturbing particles
steps.sub: The mere existence of a definite which-path fact is what destroys interference

steps.label: Turn the which-path detector back off
steps.sub: The interference pattern returns — nothing about the trajectories changed

steps.label: Every particle with momentum has an associated wavelength
steps.sub: More momentum means a shorter associated wavelength

steps.label: Confirmed directly with electron beams on crystals
steps.sub: They produce diffraction patterns matching de Broglie's predicted spacing

steps.label: Electrons aren't uniquely strange
steps.sub: Every piece of matter has a wave character, in principle

steps.label: For anything bigger than a molecule, it's unobservable
steps.sub: The wavelength is far too small compared to everyday scales

steps.label: A quantum object is described by a complex amplitude
steps.sub: Spread across every path or position available to it at once

steps.label: Amplitudes combine the way waves combine
steps.sub: Adding constructively or destructively — exactly the interference you see

steps.label: The 'particle' side only shows up at measurement
steps.sub: One definite, localized outcome — never a smeared-out half-detection

steps.label: This is quantum computing's central trick
steps.sub: Wrong-answer amplitudes cancel, right-answer amplitudes reinforce, then you measure

subtitle: The five precise rules that define what quantum mechanics actually is.
